evidence.quote: This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.

summary.short: Amends Regulation (EU) 2021/1173 to give the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking a seventh objective: acquiring, owning and operating AI-optimised supercomputers and developing AI factories, with access reserved for trustworthy AI proposals. Applies from the twentieth day after publication in the Official Journal.
summary.long: Council Regulation (EU) 2024/1732 amends Regulation (EU) 2021/1173 establishing the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC). It adds a seventh objective of developing and operating AI factories, and defines 'AI-optimised supercomputer' and 'AI factory'. The Joint Undertaking may acquire and own AI-optimised supercomputers, which must be located in a EuroHPC hosting entity or a supercomputing centre in the Union. The Union contribution covers up to 50% of acquisition costs and up to 50% of operating costs, with the remainder borne by the hosting Participating States. Supplier selection must address supply-chain security, and the Governing Board may restrict supplier participation for security reasons. Existing hosting entities may apply to become AI factories through a call for expressions of interest, and hosting entities of AI-optimised supercomputers must create a one-stop shop for users. Upgrades of EuroHPC supercomputers with AI capabilities are also permitted. AI-optimised and upgraded supercomputers are to be used primarily for large-scale AI model development and testing. Access conditions reserve eligibility for trustworthy and ethical AI proposals and include dedicated access for startups and SMEs, and the Union's share of access time may not exceed 50%. The Regulation is binding and directly applicable in all Member States and enters into force on the twentieth day after publication.

notes: Amending act: Article 1 sets out insertions and replacements in Regulation (EU) 2021/1173, coded from the Article 1 text only. Target IDs are not in the registry input, so target_instrument_id is empty for all relations. The Statutes cited in inserted Art. 12a(7) (winding up under Article 23(4) of the Statutes) are not identified in this text. The document states no publication date; Article 2 sets entry into force on the twentieth day after publication. Recital (6) links timing to the AI Act's date of application, but no operative provision states a date.

enforcement.note: This amending Council Regulation (EU) 2024/1732 adds objectives, definitions, AI factory provisions and access rules to Regulation (EU) 2021/1173. It contains no sanction, penalty, fine, licence revocation, clawback, suspension or blocking provisions. Any enforcement terms would sit in the amended regulation, which is not reproduced in this text.
